General_Description.Text: PEGASOS is a polyethylene glycol (PEG)-associated solvent-based tissue clearing method that renders nearly all types of tissues, including hard tissues like bones and teeth, transparent while preserving endogenous fluorescence. It achieves high tissue transparency through a series of steps involving fixation, decalcification, decolorization, delipidation, dehydration, and clearing. The method can be performed using either a recirculation procedure for whole-body or large body parts or a passive immersion procedure for individual organs or small body parts. The PEG component within the clearing medium provides long-term protection for endogenous fluorescence, making PEGASOS suitable for imaging complex structures such as the intact mouse head, brain, and neural networks within the marrow space of long bones.
Text_Reference: ARTICLE OPEN section: 'Here, we developed a polyethylene glycol (PEG)-associated solvent system (PEGASOS), which rendered nearly all types of tissues transparent and preserved endogenous fluorescence.'

INTRODUCTION section: 'Therefore, we designed the polyethylene glycol (PEG) associated solvent system (PEGASOS) tissue clearing method. We demonstrated that the PEGASOS method renders nearly all types of tissues transparent except pigmented epithelium. Hard tissues including bones and teeth become nearly invisible after clearing. Polyethylene glycol component within the clearing medium provided protection for endogenous fluorescence for a long time.'
RESULTS section: 'The PEGASOS recirculation method achieves whole-body transparency and enables large body part imaging without blind spots'
RESULTS section: 'PEGASOS passive immersion method efficiently clears nearly all types of tissues'
RESULTS section: 'The PEGASOS method is consisted of multiple steps including fixation, decalcification (hard tissue only), decolorization, delipidation, dehydration, and clearing.'

Tissue_Types.Text1: The PEGASOS method can efficiently clear nearly all types of soft and hard tissues, including bones, teeth, liver, spleen and heart, with the specific exception of pigmented epithelium.
Text1_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'PEGASOS achieved transparency for nearly all types of tissues including the teeth, long bone, spleen, liver, and heart.'
RESULTS section: 'We demonstrated that the PEGASOS method renders nearly all types of tissues transparent except pigmented epithelium.'

Tissue_Types.Text2: The recirculation procedure was used to render the whole body of an adult mouse transparent.
Text2_Reference: ARTICLE OPEN section: 'The PEGASOS method turned the whole adult mouse body transparent and we were able to image an adult mouse head composed of bones, teeth, brain, muscles, and other tissues with no blind areas.'

Tissue_Types.Text3: The passive immersion procedure was used to clear the whole body of a young (P7) mouse pup, achieving transparency in both soft and hard tissues.
Text3_Reference: Results Section: '...whole body of young mouse pups could be cleared following the passive immersion procedure for the hard tissue due to their smaller size. A Tie2-Cre;Ai14 mouse pup of postnatal day 7 age (P7) was cleared and showed full transparency... except the pigmented eyes...'

Tissue_Types.Text4: To validate scalability, the method was successfully applied to clear an entire adult rat (>300g), including its mandible, femur, brain, heart, liver, spleen, and kidney.
Text4_Reference: Results Section: 'To test if the PEGASOS can be scaled up for larger animal, we attempted to clear adult rats (12 weeks of age) with the recirculation procedure... Other organs including the femur, brain, heart, liver, spleen, and kidney were all efficiently cleared and showed complete transparency...'

Tissue_Types.Text5: The PEGASOS passive immersion procedure was successfully used to clear a fixed human brain sample.
Text5_Reference: Results Section: 'We attempted to clear a fixed human brain sample (3 × 3 × 1 cm) with the PEGASOS passive immersion procedure. The human brain sample turned transparent after clearing...'

Tissue_Types.Text6: The passive immersion procedure was used to clear dog tibia cortical bone(1 cm×3 mm×3 mm).
Text6_Reference: Results Section: 'A piece of dog tibia cortical bone (1 cm×3 mm×3 mm) was cleared following the passive immersion procedure for hard tissue. The bone piece turned nearly invisible after clearing...'

dog: Tibia cortical bone (1 cm×3 mm×3 mm)

Time_Consumption.Text1: Clearing mouse-sized hard tissue samples or a whole mouse body (adult or pup) typically takes approximately 12 days.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section: 'A typical recirculation clearing procedure took 12 days (Fig. 1a).'
RESULTS section: 'For hard tissue, ~12 days were needed for final clearing (Fig. 2a).'
Results Section: 'A Tie2-Cre;Ai14 mouse pup of postnatal day 7 age (P7) was cleared and showed full transparency 12 days after fixation...'

Time_Consumption.Text2: Soft tissue organs can be cleared much faster, typically within 7 days, as decalcification is not needed.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section: 'The PEGASOS passive immersion procedure could clear soft tissue organs in a much shorter time because decalcification is not needed. Within 7 days, we were able to make the brain, liver lobe, spleen, heart, kidney, stomach, intestine, and lung completely transparent...'

Time_Consumption.Text3: The entire clearing process for larger animals like adult rats took 1 month.
Text3_Reference: Both PEGASOS recirculation and passive immersion procedures can be scaled up for clearing large animal models section: 'The entire clearing process took 1 month with duration of each step being doubled.'

Tissue_Deformation.Text1: The PEGASOS method does not cause shrinkage in tested bone samples, but it causes 30% to 40% shrinkage in soft tissue organs. This shrinkage is anisotropic but does not cause detectable distortion of internal structures.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section, 'Performance comparison between the PEGASOS and other clearing methods': 'Although PEGASOS method did not lead to shrinkage of bone samples we tested, we noticed that it caused shrinkage of the soft tissue organs. The shrinkage ratio varied between 30% (heart, liver) and 40% (brain, spleen). Analysis performed on brain slices indicates that the shrinkage is anisotropic and does not cause detectable distortion of internal structures.'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text1: The method is compatible with both expressed fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP, tdTomato), retaining ~70% of original intensity, and endogenous structural signals via Second-Harmonic Generation (SHG).
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section, 'PEG component efficiently protects GFP and tdTomato fluorescence': 'At the end of PEGASOS clearing process, both GFP and tdTomato fluorescence retained ~70% of the original intensity.'
Results Section: '...3-D reconstitution showed intact head organization with both SHG and tdTomato signals...'

Fluorescence_Compatibility.Text2: The compatibility with whole-mount immunofluorescent staining was validated with a wide range of antibodies and stains, including anti-αSMA, Laminin, anti-GFAP, GS-IB4, anti-parvalbumin, and anti-Collagen IV.
Text2_Reference: Results Section: 'To evaluate if the PEGASOS method is compatible with immunohistochemical staining, we performed whole-mount immunofluorescent staining of various soft tissue organs and cleared them using the PEGASOS immersion method afterwards...'

Preservation_Stability.Text1: In the BB-PEG clearing medium, endogenous fluorescence intensity (GFP and tdTomato) increases in the first week and is maintained for at least one month, resulting in a final intensity 30-50% higher than the beginning.
Text1_Reference: RESULTS section: 'After the samples being placed in the BB-PEG medium, the endogenous fluorescence intensity increased in the first week and maintained at the same level even 1 month later. The final fluorescence intensity was 30%–50% higher than the beginning.'

Preservation_Stability.Text2: In contrast, clearing media from other methods like uDISCO or FluoClear reduced GFP and tdTomato fluorescence intensities by around 50% after one week.
Text2_Reference: RESULTS section, 'PEG component efficiently protects GFP and tdTomato fluorescence': 'In contrast, the GFP and tdTomato fluorescence intensities were reduced by around 50% 1 week after the treatment of the uDISCO or FluoClear clearing media.'

Application.Text1: The method enables visualization of neuronal structures through the skull of an adult mouse, allowing for imaging of brain organization, individual neurons at depths up to 5mm, and cranial nerves.
Text1_Reference: Results Section: '...Brain organization was clearly demonstrated by imaging through the calvarial bone... individual neurons could be visualized on sections acquired at 2, 3, and 5 mm Z-depths...Cranial nerves...were also visualized...'

Application.Text2: It was used to visualize vascular networks through hard tissues, such as vasculature within the spinal cord through a vertebra, and the vascular network encapsulated by tooth enamel and dentin.
Text2_Reference: Results Section: 'We imaged the vertebrae segment...and visualized the vasculature network within the spinal cord...'
Results Section: '...By imaging the teeth on a cleared mandible...we were able to visualize the enriched vascular network encapsulated by enamel and dentin...'

Application.Text3: PEGASOS was used for 3D reconstitution of various hard tissues based on their SHG signal, including the entire mandible with internal teeth, the entire femur revealing trabecular structure, and the knee joint showing articular surfaces and ligaments.
Text3_Reference: Results Section: 'Based on the SHG fluorescent signal, we were able to reconstitute hard tissue samples in 3-D...We reconstituted the entire mandible...We reconstituted the entire femur...We reconstituted the knee joint...'

Application.Text4: The method was applied to visualize the internal micro-architecture of multiple soft tissue organs, including the vascular organization in the liver, kidney, stomach, and intestine, and the bronchi organization in the lung.
Text4_Reference: Results Section: '...revealed the vasculature organization within the liver and kidney...'
Results Section: '...revealed the vasculatures in both [stomach and intestine]...'
Results Section: '...reveal the bronchi organization [in the lung]...'

Application.Text5: It was applied to cleared adult Thy1-EGFP mice for detailed imaging of the CNS, which included: (1) Imaging the entire CNS with DRGs through the vertebrae, (2) Visualizing individual axons and neurons, and (3) Tracing individual axons for over 2 cm.
Text5_Reference: Results Section: 'We were able to image the entire CNS together with DRGs through the vertebrae...'
Results Section: 'Individual axons and neurons could be visualized...'
Results Section: 'We were able to trace individual central axons together with their daughter branches for over 2 cm within the spinal cord...'

Application.Text6: The method was used to demonstrate, for the first time in 3D, the distribution of nerves and arteries within bone marrow, including visualizing the PNS around vertebrae, the neural network penetrating the tibia, and the comparative density of nerves versus arteries.
Text6_Reference: Results Section: '...Sympathetic ganglia, DRG, spinal nerves...were also visualized...'
Results Section: '...distribution in 3-D has never been demonstrated...visualized the neural network within the tibia bone marrow space...'
Results Section: '...quantification indicates that nerves are more enriched in the middle shaft region...whereas the artery density is higher near the growth plate...'

Application.Text7: The method was applied to study the in vivo effects of chemotherapy on MSCs, using 3D quantification to show that the drug Ara-C reduced the number of TA cells from ~7000 to ~3000, suggesting inhibited MSC activation.
Text7_Reference: Results Section: '3-D quantification indicates that incisors of PBS-treated mice contain ~7000 TA cells...In contrast, TA cell number in incisors of AraC-treated mouse reduced to ~3000...suggests that AraC treatment inhibits the activation of incisor MSCs into TA cells.'

Note.Text1: The method's primary capability gap is its inability to decolorize pigmented tissues, such as the pigment retina.
Text1_Reference: Results Section: 'In summary, the PEGASOS method efficiently cleared all types of tissues except pigment retina.'

Note.Text2: Compared to methods like 3DISCO and uDISCO, PEGASOS takes longer due to the required decalcification and decolorization steps for hard tissues.
Text2_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'PEGASOS clearing method takes longer accomplishing time as compared with 3DISCO and uDISCO, due to the incorporation of decalciﬁcation and decolorization steps.'

Note.Text3: A noted side effect is that the method significantly increases the auto-fluorescence of muscle tissue, which can deteriorate the image's signal-to-noise ratio.
Text3_Reference: DISCUSSION section: 'Shrinkage also significantly increases the auto-fluorescence of muscle tissue, which deteriorates the signal-to-noise ratio of the image.'
